title: PIVlab - Time-Resolved Digital Particle Image Velocimetry Tool for MATLAB
abstract:
PIVlab is a time-resolved particle image velocimetry (PIV) software that does not only calculate the velocity distribution within particle image pairs, but can also be used to derive, display and export multiple parameters of the flow pattern. A user-friendly graphical user interface (GUI) makes PIV analyses and data post-processing fast and efficient.
Screen-capture video of the tool:
http://vimeo.com/10090907
Example analyses & videos can be found on the PIVlab website:
http://PIVlab.blogspot.com Please ask your questions in the PIVlab forum:
http://pivlab.blogspot.de/p/forum.html Peer reviewed paper on PIVlab: Thielicke, W and Stamhuis, E.J. 2014. PIVlab – Towards User-friendly, Affordable and Accurate Digital Particle Image Velocimetry in MATLAB. Journal of Open Research Software 2(1):e30, DOI: http://dx.doi.org/10.5334/jors.bl Main features:
* completely GUI based PIV tool
* multi-pass, multi grid window deformation technique
* import bmp/ tiff/ jpeg image pairs/ series
* image sequencing styles A-B, C-D, ... or A-B, B-C, ...
* individual image masking and region of interest (ROI) selection
* image pre-processing (contrast enhancement, highpass, intensity capping)
* two different sub-pixel estimators
* multiple vector validation methods
* magnitude/ vorticity/ divergence/ shear / ...
* data smoothing, vector field highpass
* multiple colormaps
* streamlines
* extensive data extraction tools/ integration via poly lines/ circles/ area
* statistics (histograms, scatterplot, mean & stdev)
* precise particle image pair generation with user-defined parameters and several flow simulations (synthetic PIV image generator)
* data export (matlab, ascii, movie file, image, Paraview, ...)
* main features accessible via comand line scripting

narrative:
Short impact summary

PIVlab has established itself as a widely reused MATLAB-based workflow for particle image velocimetry, with 191 scholarly citations and 199 documented downstream reuses. Its influence is especially clear in fluid mechanics and related experimental fields, where it is repeatedly cited in venues such as Physics of Fluids and Experiments in Fluids.

Full narrative

PIVlab is a time-resolved digital particle image velocimetry tool designed to make flow analysis faster and more accessible through a user-friendly graphical interface. The record shows sustained scholarly uptake since publication, with citations appearing consistently across the years and continuing into recent work, indicating that the software has become a practical method anchor for researchers analyzing velocity fields and flow patterns.

The citation landscape points to broad methodological relevance within experimental fluid dynamics and adjacent areas. The strongest concentration is in journals such as Physics of Fluids, while reuse also appears in preprints, conference papers, dissertations, and book chapters. That mix suggests PIVlab is not limited to one publication pathway: it is being used both in peer-reviewed research and in earlier-stage or instructional research outputs.

Disciplinarily, the citing work spans fluid dynamics, hydrology and sediment transport, granular flows, microfluidic technologies, and vibration-related flow studies. Recent citing articles include studies of swash flows, stepped spillways, pulse jets, granular drainage, and spray or mixing phenomena, which shows that the tool is applied wherever high-quality flow-field measurement is needed rather than confined to a single niche.

The surrounding record is comparatively quiet on public discourse and event-based attention, so the clearest evidence of impact remains scholarly reuse and citation. In that context, PIVlab’s profile is strong: it is openly available through Figshare, has a documented version history, and shows repeated uptake across education-heavy and research-intensive settings. Overall, the evidence supports its role as a durable, widely adopted software method in experimental flow analysis.
